newsitem.title: USA: Arthuis complains about Balladur bond.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis complains about Balladur bond.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis on Monday criticised a 120 billion franc government bond launched in 1993, saying that the government would now have to find the money to pay it back.
The "Balladur bond", named after former prime minister Edouard Balladur, matures in 1997.

"France launched a major state loan a while ago. In 1997 that will have to be refunded. We will have to launch a new loan for an equivalent amount," Arthuis told a news conference at the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.
Officials stressed however there was no change to France's programme of state borrowings, and there was no question of launching a special bond to repay the Balladur bond.
Reimbursement of the Balladur bond has already been taken into account in France's borrowing programme for next year and will be covered through normal regular issues of government bonds.
